overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the police-station notice was reasonable given the body did not foresee a crowd and relocated promptly, no roll calls were required, and the minutes accurately reflected the meeting. The exhibit-list allegation was declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the March 5 meeting was noticed for the police station although the body knew the room could not hold the expected crowd.
allegations.key_passage: Absent sufficient evidence to the contrary, we credit the Committee’s account that it did not anticipate prior to the March 5 meeting that a larger-than-usual crowd would wish to attend the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee failed to take roll call votes at the March 5 meeting after an individual participated remotely.
Complaint alleged the March 5 minutes omit a list of documents and exhibits used at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: For the same reasons as explained in OML Declination 6-18-2025 (Northborough Housing Authority Board of Commissioners) and OML Declination 6-18-2025 (Swansea Finance and Advisory Committee), we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the minutes fail to record that the meeting was called to order at the police station or that the Committee voted to move the meeting to the high school.
allegations.key_passage: The complaint essentially alleges that the Committee failed to include in its minutes things that did not occur during the March 5 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the March 5 minutes do not record votes by roll call with the details of each member's vote.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, although we have explained that roll call votes must be recorded in meeting minutes by roll call—that is, must record the name of each member and how they voted—we have not found such a requirement for votes that are not take by roll call.
